- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer for momentum decay.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to counteract.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) followed by model overreaction — apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.3+), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by 0.5–1.0% downward for next 3–5 days.
